title: What the stopping potential measures
spoken: The electron's charge times the stopping potential equals the largest kinetic energy, which equals h times the frequency minus the escape work.
explanation: A retarding potential that just stops the fastest electrons measures their energy: charge times potential. The one-quantum budget says what that energy should be.
assumptions: One electron receives the whole of one quantum, h times the frequency, and nothing from a second quantum.
Escaping costs the electron at least the escape work; any further loss on the way out is not negative.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed section 8.
The stopping potential is taken as measured on the fastest electrons, with contact potentials between electrode materials ignored.

notes.title: Charge of one electron
notes.explanation: Charge times a potential difference is an energy: the work the field does on the electron as it crosses.

notes.title: Stopping potential
notes.explanation: The retarding potential at which the current of the fastest electrons just stops. It is read off the apparatus.

notes.title: Largest kinetic energy
notes.explanation: The energy the stopping potential measures, and the energy the one-quantum budget predicts.

notes.title: Planck's constant
notes.explanation: Sets one quantum's energy with the frequency. It is also the slope of stopping energy against frequency.

notes.title: Frequency of the light
notes.explanation: The one property of the light the stopping energy depends on in this model.

notes.title: Escape work
notes.explanation: On a plot of stopping energy against frequency the model's line crosses zero frequency at minus the escape work, so the line's intercept measures it.

notes.title: A potential measures an energy
notes.explanation: Charge times stopping potential is the energy the fastest electron had. This half is how the apparatus reads energy, not a claim about light.

notes.title: The prediction to test
notes.explanation: The one-quantum budget says that measured energy rises in a straight line with frequency, with slope h. An experiment can test that; restating the equation cannot.
